_comment: Semantic net of legal terms. 'concepts' are nodes; 'relations' are typed edges [source, relation, target]. Relations: is_a, part_of, party_to, belongs_to, requires, related_to, remedy_for, exception_to, applies_to.

concepts.label: Law
concepts.definition: The system of rules a society recognises as regulating the conduct of its members, enforced through courts and penalties.

concepts.label: Contract Law
concepts.definition: The area of law governing how agreements are made, interpreted and enforced.

concepts.label: Tort Law
concepts.definition: The area of civil law that gives remedies to people harmed by the wrongful acts or carelessness of others.

concepts.label: Criminal Law
concepts.definition: Law dealing with offences against the public or the state, punishable by fines or imprisonment.

concepts.label: Property & Tenancy Law
concepts.definition: Law governing the ownership, use and renting of land and buildings.

concepts.label: Employment Law
concepts.definition: Law governing the relationship between employers and employees, including pay, conditions and dismissal.

concepts.label: Family Law
concepts.definition: Law dealing with family relationships such as marriage, divorce and the care of children.

concepts.label: Consumer Law
concepts.definition: Law protecting buyers of goods and services against unsafe products and unfair business practices.

concepts.label: Intellectual Property Law
concepts.definition: Law protecting creations of the mind such as inventions, creative works and brand names.

concepts.label: Civil Procedure
concepts.definition: The rules courts follow in non-criminal disputes, from filing a claim to enforcing a judgment.

concepts.label: Wills & Estates
concepts.definition: Law governing how a person's property is managed and passed on after their death.

concepts.label: Contract
concepts.definition: A legally enforceable agreement between two or more parties that creates mutual obligations.

concepts.label: Offer
concepts.definition: A clear proposal by one party to enter into a contract on specific terms.

concepts.label: Acceptance
concepts.definition: Unconditional agreement to all the terms of an offer, which creates a binding contract.

concepts.label: Consideration
concepts.definition: Something of value (money, goods, services or a promise) exchanged by each party to a contract.

concepts.label: Legal Capacity
concepts.definition: The legal ability of a person to enter into a contract, e.g. being an adult of sound mind.

concepts.label: Breach of Contract
concepts.definition: Failure by a party, without lawful excuse, to perform any promise that forms part of a contract.

concepts.label: Void Contract
concepts.definition: An agreement that has no legal effect from the start, for example one made for an illegal purpose.

concepts.label: Voidable Contract
concepts.definition: A valid contract that one party may choose to cancel, e.g. because it was signed under pressure or misrepresentation.

concepts.label: Non-Disclosure Agreement
concepts.definition: A contract in which the parties agree not to disclose specified confidential information.

concepts.label: Legal Remedy
concepts.definition: The means by which a court enforces a right or compensates for a wrong.

concepts.label: Damages
concepts.definition: Money awarded by a court to compensate for loss or injury caused by another party.

concepts.label: Specific Performance
concepts.definition: A court order requiring a party to carry out their obligations under a contract.

concepts.label: Injunction
concepts.definition: A court order requiring a person to do, or stop doing, a specific act.

concepts.label: Tort
concepts.definition: A civil wrong, other than breach of contract, that causes harm and for which the injured person can claim damages.

concepts.label: Negligence
concepts.definition: Failure to take the care a reasonable person would take, causing foreseeable harm to someone owed a duty of care.

concepts.label: Duty of Care
concepts.definition: A legal obligation to take reasonable care to avoid causing foreseeable harm to others.

concepts.label: Causation
concepts.definition: The link showing that the defendant's conduct actually caused the claimant's harm.

concepts.label: Defamation
concepts.definition: A false statement presented as fact, communicated to others, that harms someone's reputation.

concepts.label: Libel
concepts.definition: Defamation in a permanent form, such as writing, print, broadcasts or online posts.

concepts.label: Slander
concepts.definition: Defamation in a spoken or otherwise transient form.

concepts.label: Nuisance
concepts.definition: Unreasonable interference with a person's use or enjoyment of their property, such as excessive noise or smells.

concepts.label: Trespass
concepts.definition: Entering or remaining on someone's land or property without permission.

concepts.label: Personal Injury
concepts.definition: Physical or psychological harm caused to a person, often through someone else's negligence.

concepts.label: Product Liability
concepts.definition: The legal responsibility of manufacturers and sellers for harm caused by defective products.

concepts.label: Crime
concepts.definition: An act or omission that the law forbids and punishes, prosecuted by the state.

concepts.label: Felony
concepts.definition: A serious crime, typically punishable by more than a year of imprisonment.

concepts.label: Misdemeanor
concepts.definition: A less serious crime, usually punished by a fine or a short jail term.

concepts.label: Theft
concepts.definition: Dishonestly taking another person's property with the intention of permanently depriving them of it.

concepts.label: Assault
concepts.definition: Intentionally causing, or threatening, unlawful physical harm to another person.

concepts.label: Fraud
concepts.definition: Deliberate deception to secure an unfair or unlawful gain, such as money or property.

concepts.label: Cybercrime
concepts.definition: Crime committed using computers or the internet, such as hacking, identity theft or online fraud.

concepts.label: Arrest
concepts.definition: Taking a person into custody by legal authority, usually on suspicion of a crime.

concepts.label: Bail
concepts.definition: Temporary release of an accused person awaiting trial, often secured by money or conditions.

concepts.label: Right to Remain Silent
concepts.definition: An accused person's right not to answer police questions that might incriminate them.

concepts.label: Lease
concepts.definition: A contract by which a landlord lets a tenant use property for a period in return for rent.

concepts.label: Landlord
concepts.definition: The owner who rents out property to a tenant.

concepts.label: Tenant
concepts.definition: A person who occupies property rented from a landlord.

concepts.label: Security Deposit
concepts.definition: Money paid by a tenant at the start of a lease to cover unpaid rent or damage, normally returned at the end.

concepts.label: Rent
concepts.definition: The periodic payment a tenant makes to a landlord for the use of property.

concepts.label: Eviction
concepts.definition: The legal process by which a landlord removes a tenant from rented property.

concepts.label: Employment Contract
concepts.definition: A contract setting out the terms of work between an employer and an employee.

concepts.label: Employer
concepts.definition: A person or organisation that hires and pays employees.

concepts.label: Employee
concepts.definition: A person who works for an employer under a contract of employment.

concepts.label: Wrongful Termination
concepts.definition: Dismissal of an employee in breach of their contract or the law, e.g. without proper notice or for a discriminatory reason.

concepts.label: Notice Period
concepts.definition: The length of advance warning an employer or employee must give before ending employment.

concepts.label: Wages & Minimum Wage
concepts.definition: Payment an employer owes an employee for work done; most jurisdictions also set a legal minimum wage.

concepts.label: Overtime
concepts.definition: Work beyond normal working hours, which often must be paid at a higher rate.

concepts.label: Workplace Harassment
concepts.definition: Unwelcome conduct at work, including sexual harassment or bullying, that creates an intimidating or hostile environment.

concepts.label: Discrimination
concepts.definition: Treating someone unfairly because of a protected characteristic such as race, sex, religion, age or disability.

concepts.label: Marriage
concepts.definition: A legally recognised union between two people that creates mutual rights and obligations.

concepts.label: Divorce
concepts.definition: The legal ending of a marriage by a court or other competent authority.

concepts.label: Child Custody
concepts.definition: The legal right and responsibility to care for, and make decisions about, a child.

concepts.label: Child Support
concepts.definition: Regular payments by a parent to help cover a child's living costs after separation.

concepts.label: Alimony
concepts.definition: Financial support paid by one spouse to the other after separation or divorce.

concepts.label: Prenuptial Agreement
concepts.definition: A contract made before marriage setting out how assets will be divided if the marriage ends.

concepts.label: Domestic Violence
concepts.definition: Abuse or violence by a partner or family member; it is a crime and grounds for a protection order.

concepts.label: Consumer Rights
concepts.definition: Legal protections giving buyers the right to safe goods, accurate information and fair remedies.

concepts.label: Warranty
concepts.definition: A guarantee by a seller or manufacturer that a product will meet certain standards for a period of time.

concepts.label: Refund
concepts.definition: Return of money to a buyer, typically for faulty goods or for services not provided as agreed.

concepts.label: Defective Goods
concepts.definition: Products that are faulty, unsafe or not as described when sold.

concepts.label: Copyright
concepts.definition: The exclusive legal right of a creator to copy, distribute and adapt an original work.

concepts.label: Trademark
concepts.definition: A protected sign, name or logo that distinguishes one business's goods or services from others.

concepts.label: Patent
concepts.definition: An exclusive right granted for an invention for a limited period, in exchange for public disclosure.

concepts.label: Fair Use / Fair Dealing
concepts.definition: A limited exception allowing use of copyrighted material without permission, e.g. for criticism, news reporting or education.

concepts.label: IP Infringement
concepts.definition: Unauthorised use of a protected intellectual property right such as a copyright, trademark or patent.

concepts.label: Lawsuit
concepts.definition: A claim brought in a civil court by one party against another, seeking a legal remedy.

concepts.label: Plaintiff
concepts.definition: The person who brings a lawsuit (also called the claimant or petitioner).

concepts.label: Defendant
concepts.definition: The person against whom a lawsuit or criminal charge is brought.

concepts.label: Statute of Limitations
concepts.definition: The legal deadline for starting a lawsuit or prosecution after an event; late claims are usually barred.

concepts.label: Small Claims Court
concepts.definition: A simplified court for low-value disputes, where parties can often appear without a lawyer.

concepts.label: Alternative Dispute Resolution
concepts.definition: Ways of resolving disputes outside court, such as mediation and arbitration.

concepts.label: Mediation
concepts.definition: A voluntary process in which a neutral mediator helps the parties reach their own settlement.

concepts.label: Arbitration
concepts.definition: Private dispute resolution in which a neutral arbitrator makes a binding decision.

concepts.label: Legal Notice
concepts.definition: A formal written communication informing a party of a legal claim and the action intended if it is not resolved.

concepts.label: Evidence
concepts.definition: Information such as documents, photos, recordings or testimony used to prove facts in a case.

concepts.label: Affidavit
concepts.definition: A written statement of facts sworn under oath before an authorised official.

concepts.label: Lawyer
concepts.definition: A qualified professional who advises clients and represents them in legal matters.

concepts.label: Legal Aid
concepts.definition: Free or low-cost legal help for people who cannot afford a lawyer.

concepts.label: Power of Attorney
concepts.definition: A legal document authorising someone to act on another person's behalf in legal or financial matters.

concepts.label: Will
concepts.definition: A legal document stating how a person's property should be distributed after their death.

concepts.label: Executor
concepts.definition: The person named in a will to carry out its instructions and administer the estate.

concepts.label: Probate
concepts.definition: The court process of validating a will and authorising the administration of a deceased person's estate.

concepts.label: Inheritance
concepts.definition: Property received from someone who has died, either under a will or by law.

concepts.label: Constitutional Law
concepts.definition: The area of law dealing with a country's constitution: how the state is organised, the limits on government power, and citizens' fundamental rights.

concepts.label: Legal System & Courts
concepts.definition: How laws are made, interpreted and applied: legislatures, courts, judges and the principles that guide them.

concepts.label: Civil Law
concepts.definition: The branch of law that settles disputes between private parties (people or organisations), usually by ordering compensation or another remedy rather than punishment.

concepts.label: Court
concepts.definition: A body with legal authority to hear disputes, decide cases and enforce the law.

concepts.label: Judge
concepts.definition: A public officer appointed to hear cases in court and decide them impartially according to the law.

concepts.label: Supreme Court
concepts.definition: The highest court of a country; its decisions bind all other courts. In India it can also be approached directly to enforce fundamental rights (Article 32).

concepts.label: High Court
concepts.definition: In India, the highest court of a state or group of states; it hears appeals from lower courts and can issue writs to enforce rights (Article 226).

concepts.label: Jurisdiction
concepts.definition: The authority of a court or body to hear a particular case, decided by where the matter arose, its subject and the value of the claim.

concepts.label: Legislation
concepts.definition: Written law made by a legislature such as Parliament or a state assembly; a single law is called an Act or statute.

concepts.label: Precedent
concepts.definition: An earlier court decision that guides or binds courts deciding similar cases later; decisions of higher courts bind lower courts.

concepts.label: Appeal
concepts.definition: A request to a higher court to review and change a lower court's decision.

concepts.label: Verdict (Judgment)
concepts.definition: A court's decision in a case, stating the result and the reasons for it.

concepts.label: Justice
concepts.definition: Fair and impartial treatment under the law: rights are protected, wrongs are remedied and everyone is treated equally.

concepts.label: Legal Right
concepts.definition: An interest or claim that the law recognises and protects, which others have a legal duty to respect.

concepts.label: Lok Adalat
concepts.definition: A 'people's court' in India where pending or new disputes are settled by compromise; there is no court fee and the award is final and binding.

concepts.label: Constitution
concepts.definition: The supreme law of a country: it sets out how government is organised, the powers of each branch and the fundamental rights of citizens. India's Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950.

concepts.label: Fundamental Rights
concepts.definition: Basic rights guaranteed by the Constitution and enforceable in court. In India (Part III) they cover equality, freedoms, protection against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and the right to constitutional remedies.

concepts.label: Right to Equality
concepts.definition: The right to equality before the law and protection from discrimination on grounds such as religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth (Articles 14 to 18 of India's Constitution).

concepts.label: Freedom of Speech and Expression
concepts.definition: The right to express opinions freely, subject to reasonable restrictions such as public order, decency, defamation and national security (Article 19 in India).

concepts.label: Right to Life and Personal Liberty
concepts.definition: The right not to be deprived of life or personal liberty except by a fair, just and reasonable legal procedure (Article 21 in India). Courts have held that it includes privacy, dignity and a speedy trial.

concepts.label: Writ
concepts.definition: A court order enforcing rights or controlling public authorities: habeas corpus (produce a detained person), mandamus (perform a duty), prohibition, certiorari and quo warranto. In India, issued by the Supreme Court (Article 32) and High Courts (Article 226).

concepts.label: Public Interest Litigation (PIL)
concepts.definition: A case filed in court to protect the public interest or the rights of people who cannot approach the court themselves.

concepts.label: Directive Principles of State Policy
concepts.definition: Guidelines in Part IV of India's Constitution for the government when making laws and policy, such as welfare and equal pay; they are not enforceable in court.

concepts.label: Fundamental Duties
concepts.definition: Duties of every citizen listed in Article 51A of India's Constitution, such as respecting the Constitution, the national flag and the national anthem.

concepts.label: Rule of Law
concepts.definition: The principle that everyone, including the government, is subject to the same laws, applied fairly by independent courts.

concepts.label: Right to Information (RTI)
concepts.definition: A citizen's legal right to request information held by public authorities; in India it is given by the Right to Information Act, 2005.

concepts.label: FIR (First Information Report)
concepts.definition: The written record police make when they receive information about a cognizable offence; it starts the criminal investigation. In India it is registered under section 173 of the BNSS (formerly section 154 of the CrPC).

concepts.label: Zero FIR
concepts.definition: An FIR that any police station must register, whatever the place of the offence; it is then transferred to the station with jurisdiction.

concepts.label: Cognizable Offence
concepts.definition: A serious offence for which police can arrest without a warrant and investigate without a magistrate's permission, such as murder, rape or theft.

concepts.label: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)
concepts.definition: India's main criminal code, defining offences and their punishments. It replaced the Indian Penal Code (IPC) from 1 July 2024.

concepts.label: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)
concepts.definition: India's code of criminal procedure, covering FIRs, arrest, investigation, bail and trial. It replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) from 1 July 2024.

concepts.label: Anticipatory Bail
concepts.definition: A court direction that a person who fears arrest for a non-bailable offence is released on bail if arrested (section 482 BNSS, formerly section 438 CrPC).

concepts.label: Chargesheet
concepts.definition: The final report police file in court after an investigation, naming the accused and setting out the evidence against them.

concepts.label: Cheque Bounce
concepts.definition: When a cheque is returned unpaid, for example for insufficient funds. In India it is an offence under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.

concepts.label: Dowry
concepts.definition: Money, property or valuables demanded from a bride's family in connection with marriage. Giving, taking or demanding dowry is a crime in India under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

concepts.label: Consumer Commission
concepts.definition: India's consumer courts under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019: District, State and National Commissions, chosen by the value of the goods or services.
